claims.statement: Model settings observations are accepted only while native settings, exact task ownership and account/process source identity remain current.

Native Goal edits bind the current owned thread and reviewed Goal identity, require an explicit initial status, delegate budget/status policy to native execution, and materialize long objective content through native attachments.

Search preferences distinguish saved user-layer values from effective project defaults and write only web_search with native version checking and reload disabled; existing conversations are not restarted, resumed or forked for that change.
Agent memory availability is read from the native memories feature observation rather than a separate local memory configuration owner.

The attested launch requests native child context limits, Agent message wakeups and dotted fork-prefix preservation while preserving native multi-agent and transport selection. It omits the removed description-first feature.

Cold resume inherits saved native settings without creation overrides, and model-only updates omit tier, provider and collaboration settings. Exact-artifact probes cover tier/summary recovery and acknowledged approval/reviewer/read-only permissions despite stale context across fork and cold resume in legacy and paginated history, without installed-app acceptance.

The repository-owned large_catalog.py probe checks native model/list with an explicit catalog larger than 1 MiB. Current qualification identifies the selected artifact and names only probes actually executed in that batch. Earlier catalog executions retain their original artifact limits in the stable contract catalog. This adds no account or provider setup control.

The composer shield changes native permissions for the selected conversation; Settings > Agents defines new-conversation defaults with the same presets. Native children inherit parent settings, global Guardian only controls Review Details, and Speed stays in the model menu.
Native model metadata and configuration determine the helper backend; the qualified synthetic matrix uses V1 and V2 at Medium without Ultra and leaves model judgment unmeasured.

Agent preferences reads the loaded native memory summary explicitly through thread/memory/read, preserves native version selection and empty/unavailable states, copies original text only on action and invalidates replaced sources. It neither resumes nor writes/generates memory, and uses source/digest-bound 8 KiB pages up to 1 MiB.

Agent preferences and Work details show retained native usage with explicit source coverage; linked unshared turns do not establish billing, complete Work cost or elapsed time and missing history or child evidence remains unknown.

Side chats preserve source provider and Goal ownership without sending. Current qualification checks saved-provider continuation and ordinary and attached forks on the selected artifact; original explicit recovery and branch proof keep their historical limits. HumanCommand remains user-deferred and unsupported.

The Agent model catalog refreshes through native model/list every 60 seconds, with account, directory and process binding. Model and effort cycling have no fixed fallback list when the catalog is unavailable.

An explicit past native retirement deadline selects the same complete catalog's current default for new Agent settings, new Agents in a shared process and loaded idle recovery, preserving shared config and existing settings journal/readback. Missing entries, upgrade suggestions, network errors or quota responses alone do not trigger migration. Original regression groups and acceptance limits remain in the stable catalog.

Existing account/source-bound context controls expose background compaction, retention of marked client tool outputs and each configured MCP server's cached catalog. Omitted context feature values use native defaultEnabled; explicit effective config wins. Saved user values remain separate from project overrides and catalog enablement in another cwd. Saving does not restart loaded conversations or create a second config store.

The enabled-by-default automatic suggestion preference can restore a suggestion for the latest completed answer after restart, reopen or re-enabling. It preserves draft content and uses Tab only for an undoable unsent edit.

The composer and Menu Bar prefer native conversation dollars and can display an API-equivalent text-token estimate when those amounts are absent. Amounts retain source-account identity, mark incomplete coverage, and do not establish an account total or subscription charge.

The provider mismatch observation identifies source and current providers under the exact account/process/thread guards; explicit current-provider fork rechecks native configuration without changing global settings or automatically sending input.

Ordinary forks and Side chats forward current reported native model, reasoning effort and service tier, including an explicit default tier, through the bounded fork bridge; explicit provider recovery uses target defaults without source model or effort overrides.

Components installs managed RAGFlow nightly with compatible Infinity and a private service account, sharing actual version and lifecycle controls. Operations check a running Docker-compatible engine and Docker Compose without installing or launching a container runtime. Successful installation without saved models opens setup. The saved summary offers Edit; the editor uses one shared OpenAI-compatible Base URL and optional private API key with extraction and embedding model IDs. Save verifies both choices, updates their provider instances and initializes Memory. A blank key retains the saved extraction connection key only while the shared URL is unchanged; indexed Memory retains its embedding model and endpoint. New connections enable Automatic learning; existing connections keep the saved choice. Update preserves models, the learning choice and data. Reset preserves the learning choice and starts a fresh export boundary. Uninstall clears the connection while retaining data. Typed knowledge scopes and native-memory context policy retain their existing owners.

The RAGFlow status light distinguishes service installation from configured Memory without a repeated caption. Recovery guidance stays inside expanded details. A saved Models summary aligns the shared URL, model IDs and key status and keeps Edit available. The four-field editor places shared connection fields above extraction and embedding model IDs with labels above 24-point inputs. Empty required fields disable Save; explicit submission validates complete input. Editing clears the old editor error. Collapse retains unsaved input; Cancel discards the draft and errors and returns to the saved summary while RAGFlow stays expanded. API compatibility, model roles, native-memory effects and chat-import guidance remain visible.

All Settings categories share a 620-point content column and compact Settings typography. Related preferences share a quiet bordered panel with distinct section, name, value and explanation roles. Ordinary setting names use normal weight; section titles use medium weight and muted text. Accounts keeps one compact divided list surface; Add account and model verification use shared primary buttons. Help explains a choice, scope, cost, data effect, compatibility limit or recovery action. Component rows retain full reported versions. Component, MCP and Diagnostics details use a shared inset region. Diagnostics shows one overall status and three group summaries, with all individual checks in Technical details; uniform groups share a heading status and mixed groups retain item states. Local feedback keeps its compact inset icon, tone fill, centered alignment and adjacent recovery. Codex setup failures retain their original details and use Install or Reinstall through the existing preparation owner.

Settings > Agents > New conversations uses two compact rows with visible explanations. Permissions shows the selected mode's meaning and opens a menu with all four descriptions and the native Subagent inheritance rule. Speed reuses the Standard, Fast and Ultrafast segmented control, with selected-speed usage and credit multipliers visible in its row. Arrow keys cycle within permission options, Escape restores trigger focus, Tab and Shift-Tab continue navigation after dismissing the menu, and Command-W closes Settings.

The app version and Check for updates action are in Settings > General > Updates. There is no separate Updates page, and Sparkle retains application update ownership; component lifecycle actions remain in Components.

Tool catalog cache uses the shared interruptible 200 ms Settings disclosure animation in both Settings and Agent preferences. Moving details measure current content before sibling layout and clip it to revealed bounds. Expansion, collapse and server-list refresh do not save configuration.
Appearance shows all theme previews in the Settings page's single scroll area. Names wrap rather than truncate, and Color scheme help is shown when System is selected.

Current local execution settings carry one exact service tier without a duplicate fast flag. New-conversation drafts include explicit creation intent, and each submitted ordinary turn includes its overrides object.
Menu-bar visibility and automatic recap preferences belong to the App-local preference store without service-snapshot import. The service owns quota activation preferences.
The Assistant RAGFlow connection stores only a private component credential reference bound to its origin, with no service environment-variable credential path.

Codex prepares automatically in the background at local bundled App startup. Components shares that state without a permanent Verify control or generic Retry action. An interrupted first download returns to Install, and an installed private runtime offers Reinstall through the existing preparation flow. Expanded help explains startup preparation and version updates through Decodex. EGM help explains using it in an Agent chat to draft or review a design and starting a new conversation after installation or update.

Automatic learning exports only the original user input and final Assistant replies from completed Assistant exchanges and excludes tool output, reasoning, commentary and exchanges with recognized credentials. Bounded scoped automatic recall precedes ordinary Assistant input; project Agents have neither these tools nor automatic personal-memory context.
Settings uses 11.5-point labels and values, 10.5-point help, 12-point section headings and 16-point titles; expanded account metrics distinguish muted keys from primary-color values.

An idle Assistant without a native thread uses initial model discovery; the model starts empty and explicitly unavailable catalogs display an em dash. Ultrafast uses the supplied double-bolt silhouette with the current Decodex theme accent color.

Account settings separates the explained New conversations selection row from list controls and a text Show emails action; unbound conversations show a quiet Context defaults connection explanation instead of a failed native read.
Native model popovers stay transparent until final geometry and their drawable are ready, including when content height changes.

For an automatic suggestion after restart, the service can load an exact dormant native source with thread/resume before sampling and rechecks ownership afterward; it will not load an unloaded active native goal or submit parent input.
The native source requirement records upstream commit 392ced7d3a9160fd35d40c606359869215f50522, and automatic desktop suggestions require a successful completed answer and an empty editor.

The API-equivalent estimator prices recorded request tokens with their saved model selection and service tier, does not count repeated cumulative counters twice, and marks missing history, unsupported prices and cache-retention uncertainty as partial coverage.

The service starts with a bundled official price catalog and a local cache. It refreshes the official Markdown table in the background after one day, retains valid prices on refresh failure, and waits one hour before another failed-refresh attempt.
